newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian business conditions still subdued - NAB.
newsitem.headline: Australian business conditions still subdued - NAB.

text.p: Business conditions in the Australian economy remain disparate across sectors and a generalised pick up in activity has not yet occurred, according to the National Australia Bank (NAB) monthly business survey.
The April survey, the first in a new monthly series which will complement the existing quarterly NAB survey, also found that the labour market remained fundamentally weak.

The NAB's composite index of business conditions fell to negative five points in April from negative four in the March quarter. Business confidence also slipped, down to 12.4 points from 14.0 in the March quarter.
"While services continue to perform relatively well, manufacturing, retailing and wholesaling continue to report poor conditions," a commentary on the the survey said.
While the survey showed trading conditions had improved a little recently, the employment index weakened five points to negative seven and profitability conditions dropped a point to negative nine.

NAB said the employment index suggested official data may have tended to understate employment growth, but it said the poor outcome in the April survey "at the very least, points to a still fundamentally weak labour market."
Firms continued to report a build up in stocks during April, led by construction, manufacturing and wholesaling, while forward orders fell slightly after modest rises in the previous two quarters.

The survey found that while margins in the retail sector remained under downward pressure, implying little increase in underlying inflation, labour costs increased maginally, with most pressure in the manufacturing and transport sectors.
The survey also found that capacity utilisation was well below full capacity levels, reflecting subdued conditions.
